From 5a6baf204610589f8a5b5a1cd69d1fe661d9d3cd Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Luis Henriques <luis@igalia.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 14:48:30 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] fuse: fix uninit-value in fuse_dentry_revalidate()

fuse_dentry_revalidate() may be called with a dentry that didn't had
->d_time initialised.  The issue was found with KMSAN, where lookup_open()
calls __d_alloc(), followed by d_revalidate(), as shown below:

=====================================================
BUG: KMSAN: uninit-value in fuse_dentry_revalidate+0x150/0x13d0 fs/fuse/dir.c:394

 d_revalidate fs/namei.c:1030 [inline]
 lookup_open fs/namei.c:4405 [inline]
 open_last_lookups fs/namei.c:4583 [inline]
 path_openat+0x1614/0x64c0 fs/namei.c:4827
 do_file_open+0x2aa/0x680 fs/namei.c:4859
[...]

Uninit was created at:
 slab_post_alloc_hook mm/slub.c:4466 [inline]
 slab_alloc_node mm/slub.c:4788 [inline]
 kmem_cache_alloc_lru_noprof+0x382/0x1280 mm/slub.c:4807
 __d_alloc+0x55/0xa00 fs/dcache.c:1740
 d_alloc_parallel+0x99/0x2740 fs/dcache.c:2604
 lookup_open fs/namei.c:4398 [inline]
 open_last_lookups fs/namei.c:4583 [inline]
 path_openat+0x135f/0x64c0 fs/namei.c:4827
 do_file_open+0x2aa/0x680 fs/namei.c:4859
[...]
=====================================================

Reported-by: syzbot+fdebb2dc960aa56c600a@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/all/69917e0d.050a0220.340abe.02e2.GAE@google.com
Fixes: 2396356a945b ("fuse: add more control over cache invalidation behaviour")
Signed-off-by: Luis Henriques <luis@igalia.com>
Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>

diff --git a/fs/fuse/dir.c b/fs/fuse/dir.c
index 70d3e631266e..b658b6baf72f 100644
--- a/fs/fuse/dir.c
+++ b/fs/fuse/dir.c
@@ -480,6 +480,11 @@ static int fuse_dentry_init(struct dentry *dentry)
 	fd->dentry = dentry;
 	RB_CLEAR_NODE(&fd->node);
 	dentry->d_fsdata = fd;
+	/*
+	 * Initialising d_time (epoch) to '0' ensures the dentry is invalid
+	 * if compared to fc->epoch, which is initialized to '1'.
+	 */
+	dentry->d_time = 0;
 
 	return 0;
 }
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes an uninitialized-value bug in `fuse_dentry_revalidate()` where a dentry's `d_time` field was read before being set. The single modification in `fs/fuse/dir.c` adds an explicit initialization of `dentry->d_time = 0` in the `fuse_dentry_init()` function. This ensures that newly allocated dentries have a valid `d_time` value (0), which will be considered invalid compared to the fuse connection's epoch (initialized to 1), preventing the use of an uninitialized value and the associated KMSAN warning.

Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/all/69917e0d.050a0220.340abe.02e2.GAE@google.com
Fixes: 2396356a945b ("fuse: add more control over cache invalidation behaviour")
Signed-off-by: Luis Henriques <luis@igalia.com>
Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>

Here is the root cause:
fuse_dentry_revalidate() reads dentry->d_time without it being initialized when the dentry is newly allocated (e.g., during lookup_open), causing an uninitialized value access.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int fuse_dentry_init(struct dentry *dentry)
 {
 	struct fuse_dentry *fd;
 
 	fd = kzalloc_obj(struct fuse_dentry,
 			 GFP_KERNEL_ACCOUNT | __GFP_RECLAIMABLE);
 	if (!fd)
 		return -ENOMEM;
 
 	fd->dentry = dentry;
 	RB_CLEAR_NODE(&fd->node);
 	dentry->d_fsdata = fd;
+	/*
+	 * Initialising d_time (epoch) to '0' ensures the dentry is invalid
+	 * if compared to fc->epoch, which is initialized to '1'.
+	 */
+	dentry->d_time = 0;
 
 	return 0;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
In `fuse_dentry_revalidate()` (fs/fuse/dir.c), the line that reads `dentry->d_time` (likely a comparison such as `if (dentry->d_time != fc->epoch)` at line 394).
Reason:
This read occurs on a dentry that was newly allocated (e.g., by `__d_alloc` in `lookup_open`) without `dentry->d_time` being initialized. The missing initialization in `fuse_dentry_init()` causes an uninitialized value to be read, resulting in the KMSAN bug.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
In `fuse_dentry_init()` (fs/fuse/dir.c), the added line:
```c
dentry->d_time = 0;
```
Reason:
Initializing `dentry->d_time` to 0 ensures that the dentry is treated as invalid when compared to `fc->epoch`, which is initialized to 1. This prevents the uninitialized value read in `fuse_dentry_revalidate()` and eliminates the bug.
